claim:param-space-equilibria-and-nullcli.proposition:
The 2-neuron center-crossing circuit has a single unstable interior
equilibrium and oscillates — a minimal central pattern generator.
claim:param-space-equilibria-and-nullcli.hypothesis:
The two nullclines intersect at a single interior equilibrium whose Jacobian
has eigenvalues with positive real part, so the circuit does not settle but
sustains a limit-cycle oscillation.

claim:param-space-codim1-bifurcations.proposition:
On the center-crossing (symmetric, θ=−w/2) slice, a single neuron undergoes a
pitchfork bifurcation at w≈4 from 1 to 3 equilibria as self-weight grows,
reproducing Beer (2006). Off this slice the pitchfork unfolds into saddle-node
folds (see the codim-2 study).
claim:param-space-codim1-bifurcations.hypothesis:
On the center-crossing (symmetric) slice, the neuron has one equilibrium at low
self-weight and, past a pitchfork at w≈4, three equilibria (two stable, one
unstable) — the codimension-1 bifurcation structure of Beer (2006). The central
equilibrium (output 0.5) loses stability and two symmetric stable equilibria
appear.

claim:param-space-codim2-structure.proposition:
Bistability occupies a connected cusp wedge in (self-weight, bias), reproducing
the codim-2 structure of Beer (2022).
claim:param-space-codim2-structure.hypothesis:
Two saddle-node fold curves meet at a cusp and bound a connected wedge of
bistability (three equilibria) that opens as self-weight increases; the
center-crossing pitchfork is the cusp's symmetric axis — the codimension-2 organising structure of
Beer (2022).

narrative.question:
How is the dynamical repertoire of a small continuous-time recurrent neural
network (CTRNN) — the "brain" shared by all of Beer's brain-body-environment
agents — organized as a function of its parameters (self-weights and biases)?
Where do equilibria appear and disappear, and what is the codimension-1 and
codimension-2 structure of those bifurcations?
